items.title: Medical publishing in the era of artificial intelligence
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into medical research and publishing represents a transformative shift, offering unprecedented opportunities to streamline workflow efficiency, enhance language clarity, and accelerate scientific dissemination. However, this rapid technological adoption introduces ethical, epistemological, and procedural challenges, including concerns over data fabrication, automated bias, intellectual property infringement, and the erosion of scholarly accountability. A structured analysis of practical applications highlights a clear demarcation between acceptable supplementary uses and strictly prohibited practices. AI tools are unacceptable as co-authors, as authorship demands moral, legal, and scholarly accountability that non-human entities cannot possess. Similarly, generating or modifying clinical images and media using AI remains unacceptable due to the risk of data distortion and misrepresentation. Within the editorial domain, AI systems must not replace peer reviewers or editorial decision-makers. Uploading confidential manuscript content into external AI platforms violates author confidentiality, while automated algorithms lack the contextual judgment and critical reasoning necessary for peer evaluation and final publication decisions. Conversely, AI tools are acceptable for planning the structure of a manuscript, language and grammar corrections, translation, quantitative or qualitative data analysis, and formatting, provided their use is transparently disclosed and critically evaluated by human researchers. Ultimately, the ethical deployment of AI in medical literature hinges on the principle that technology must serve as an auxiliary tool rather than a replacement for human cognition. Human authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors retain full responsibility and accountability for the accuracy, integrity, and scientific validity of published work.

items.title: Memoria persistente del agente: el dato que sigue en la siguiente sesión / Persistent agent memory: the data that is still there in the next session
items.abstract: Los asistentes de consumo recuerdan entre sesiones, y los papers de agentes tratan esa memoria como un módulo de capacidad. Este artículo pregunta si esa memoria se documenta como un almacén con controles de escritura, lectura y borrado, o como un estado cuya promesa de olvido no está especificada ni medida. Se leyeron en texto crudo nueve papers, seis páginas de producto de cuatro proveedores y tres textos de autoridades de protección de datos. Las arquitecturas publican recuerdo: con GPT-4, MemGPT pasa del 32,1 % al 92,5 % de accuracy en recuperación profunda y guarda lo desalojado de forma indefinida; LongMemEval midió en agosto de 2024 que ChatGPT con GPT-4o acertaba 0,5773 frente a 0,9184 leyendo el historial completo. Ninguno de esos papers mide el borrado; un benchmark posterior sí lo mide sobre Mem0 y A-Mem como métodos. Los estudios de inserción muestran efectos en prototipos y dependen de su supuesto: AgentPoison asume acceso parcial a la base y logra un ASR medio de al menos el 80 %; MINJA no escribe el banco, pero asume un banco compartido entre usuarios, y obtiene un 76,8 % de ASR medio; en un agente clínico, unas memorias legítimas previas bajan el ASR de GPT-4o-mini del 62 % al 6,67 %. Donde el borrado sí se mide, falla o no es físico: borrar el registro deja la fuga igual que no hacer nada (any-leak 0,86–1,00), y GateMem solo mide olvido en la interfaz. Las fichas ofrecen ver, borrar y apagar, y declaran plazos —30 días para logs de OpenAI, 28 días de inactividad en Copilot Studio— sin prueba de tercero en lo leído. La contribución es separar memoria de tarea y memoria de almacén, y tres estados del borrado: no especificado, especificado y no medido, y medido y fallido. English abstract: Consumer assistants remember across sessions, and agent papers treat that memory as a capability module. This paper asks whether such memory is documented as a store with write, read and deletion controls, or as a state whose promise of forgetting is neither specified nor measured. Nine papers, six product pages from four vendors and three texts from data-protection authorities were read in raw text. The architectures report recall: with GPT-4, MemGPT goes from 32.1% to 92.5% accuracy on deep memory retrieval and keeps evicted messages indefinitely; in August 2024 LongMemEval measured ChatGPT with GPT-4o at 0.5773 versus 0.9184 when reading the full history. None of those papers measures deletion; a later benchmark does measure it on Mem0 and A-Mem as methods. Insertion studies show effects on prototypes and depend on their assumption: AgentPoison assumes partial access to the database and reaches an average ASR of at least 80%; MINJA does not write the bank but assumes a bank shared across users, and obtains an average ASR of 76.8%; in a clinical agent, pre-existing legitimate memories lower GPT-4o-mini's ASR from 62% to 6.67%. Where deletion is measured, it fails or is not physical: deleting the record leaves leakage as if nothing had been done (any-leak 0.86–1.00), and GateMem measures only interface-level forgetting. The help pages offer view, delete and turn off, and state periods—30 days for OpenAI logs, 28 days of inactivity in Copilot Studio—with no third-party test in what was read. The contribution is to separate task memory from store memory, and three states of deletion: not specified, specified but not measured, and measured and failed. Working paper de la serie WHITE-PAPERS (wp-2026-044, v0.9). Incluye versión en español e inglés. No revisado por pares. Uso de herramientas de IA declarado en el manuscrito; sin conflictos de interés ni financiación.

items.title: Metric Alignment for Hit-to-Lead Molecular Optimization with an Iterative Large Language Model Agent
items.abstract: Hit-to-lead optimization must balance binding-related performance with drug-likeness, synthetic accessibility, and early safety considerations. We developed an iterative large language model agent that integrates target and starting-hit context, literature and computational tools, multi-property scoring, and feedback from previously scored analogs. A matched benchmark covered six kinase targets, five comparison strategies, a 40-candidate budget, and six independent campaigns per method. The agent achieved the highest mean aggregate score on four targets under an objective combining docking, quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED), synthetic accessibility, and a rule-based property panel. Re-evaluating the same candidate sets using drug-likeness-gated docking and docking-drug-likeness hypervolume produced different target-level winners, showing that metric choice changes the comparative interpretation of optimization campaigns. Candidate distributions showed higher-QED regions alongside improved docking, and ablation identified scored-candidate feedback as the most consistent contributor. In an epidermal growth factor receptor campaign, an erlotinib analog retained the 4-anilinoquinazoline core while improving docking from -6.80 to approximately -8.6 kcal mol⁻¹ and QED from 0.418 to approximately 0.73. These computational results support target-specific agent evaluation and candidate prioritization for subsequent biochemical, cellular, and ADMET characterization.

items.title: Mobile Location-based Recommendation Systems and Local Businesses: Evidence from the Restaurant Industry
items.abstract: We investigate the impact of mobile location-based recommendation systems (MLBRS) on the performance of local businesses. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset of 16,720 restaurants and quasi-experimental variation generated by the official launch of a leading MLBRS, we employ a 2-Stage Least Squares instrumental-variable framework to estimate the effect of algorithmic exposure on consumer engagement. Our analysis reveals that a 1% increase in exposure is associated with a 0.078% increase in clicks; separately, a 1% increase in clicks is associated with a 0.053% increase in visit intentions. Importantly, the estimated exposure effect is larger for geographically disadvantaged restaurants, but primarily at the discovery stage (clicks). This pattern highlights a boundary condition of MLBRS: algorithmic visibility can aid, but it does not by itself resolve the uncertainty involved in acting on a recommendation. Downstream conversion is stronger when restaurants provide richer digital information and reputation signals, including consumer reviews and owner-curated information such as photos and menus. Auxiliary credit-card sales data from a restricted Seoul subsample provide consistent evidence of a positive association between algorithmic exposure and revenue, suggesting that MLBRS can shape the connection of online recommendations to offline economic outcomes.

items.title: Moda algorítmica
items.abstract: This article analyzes how digital platforms, algorithmic systems, and massive data analysis reconfigure the production and circulation of contemporary fashion. It adopts a critical-interpretive qualitative approach, combining systematic literature review, documentary analysis, and examination of empirical cases of platforms such as TikTok and SHEIN. The results evidence the emergence of a sociotechnical regime in which algorithms participate in the identification, amplification, and materialization of aesthetic trends, shifting fashion from a purely symbolic system to a hybrid ecology that articulates cultural practices and computational infrastructures. Tensions are identified between technological innovation and aesthetic standardization, productive acceleration and environmental impacts, concentration of power in platforms and possibilities for creative resistance. It is concluded that algorithmic fashion requires new analytical approaches capable of integrating culture, technology, and governance in the study of contemporary aesthetic transformations.

items.title: Monetisation Models for Academic Creators: A Mixed-Methods Study of 997 Doctorate-Signed Newsletters and 92 Public Discussion Threads
items.abstract: Scholars who publish for the public increasingly try to earn from that work, and generative AI tools promise to cut the hours it takes. This study proposes a mixed-methods framework for describing how academic creators monetise their expertise and how AI tools could change the economics, and applies it to public evidence. A quantitative strand classified the latest posts of 174,656 active newsletters on a large publishing platform, 997 of them signed by authors with a doctoral or professorial title; a qualitative strand coded 92 public question threads with 357 answers in which academics discussed earning from their expertise. One doctorate-signed newsletter in five mentioned an offer of its own, more often than other newsletters in the same topic category (odds ratio 1.47), usually through a single model such as books, courses or paid membership, whereas sponsorship and donations were rare. AI was discussed by 31% of the doctorate-signed newsletters, but only 0.6% described using it in their own work, and naming AI tools was not associated with more offers or more frequent posting. The threads raised employer policy, ethics and tax as the main concerns, and AI appeared in only one of them. A labelled planning simulation suggests that AI drafting mainly saves hours rather than raising income, and pays off most for creators with little time. A protocol for the survey and interviews, with their sample sizes, is proposed.

items.title: Multi-agent system of an energy building for prediction and learning activities
items.abstract: The rise in energy prices has intensified the need to improve the energy management in office buildings. To address this challenge, building owners often require forecasting techniques capable of supporting energy-management decisions. Forecasting can help reduce energy consumption during peak periods and support optimization strategies that improve the balance between electricity demand and supply. Several forecasting algorithms can be considered for this purpose, with different advantages and limitations, including Artificial Intelligence methods such as Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Machine Learning methods such as K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), ensemble learning methods such as eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) and Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and time-series forecasting methods such as Prophet. This paper presents a multi-agent system designed to address forecasting activities in an office building. The proposed architecture enables multiple stakeholders and specialized agents to interact while encapsulating the procedures performed by each agent For example, the building owner can request forecasts from a forecast provider without requiring access to the internal forecasting procedures performed by the forecasting agents. Other specialized agents are responsible for preparing the dataset for forecasting, calculating forecasting errors, and selecting forecasting algorithms. In addition, a learner agent uses a multi-armed bandit approach to dynamically select the forecasting algorithm for each five-minute period. The proposed architecture therefore combines modular forecasting agents, error analysis, and learning-based algorithm selection within a distributed multi-agent system.

items.title: Multidimensional effects of a school-based martial arts intervention on physical fitness, executive function, and psychological resilience in adolescents: a quasi-experimental study
items.abstract: Background Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical fitness, executive function, and psychological resilience are closely interconnected. School-based martial arts training may provide a multidimensional intervention approach by combining physical exercise, cognitive engagement, self-regulation, and psychosocial development. This study examined the effects of a 12-week school-based martial arts intervention on physical fitness, executive function, psychological resilience, self-regulation, and perceived stress among adolescents. Methods A quasi-experimental repeated-measures design was adopted. A total of 120 adolescents aged 13–16 years from three middle schools in Nanchang, China, were allocated into three groups: School-Based Martial Arts Training Group (SMATG; n = 40), Traditional Physical Education Group (TPEG; n = 40), and Control Group (CG; n = 40). The intervention was conducted three times per week for 60 min per session over 12 weeks. Outcome variables included agility, dynamic balance, muscular power, cardiorespiratory endurance, inhibitory control, working memory, cognitive flexibility, psychological resilience, self-regulation, and perceived stress. Assessments were conducted at baseline, 6 weeks, and 12 weeks. Data were analyzed using Mixed MANOVA and Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons. Results Significant Group × Time interaction effects were found across all physical, cognitive, and psychological outcomes ( p < 0.001). Compared with the TPEG and CG, the SMATG showed greater improvements in agility, dynamic balance, standing broad jump performance, Estimated VO₂peak, inhibitory control, working memory, cognitive flexibility, psychological resilience, and self-regulation, as well as greater reductions in perceived stress. Moderate-to-large effect sizes were observed across multidimensional outcomes. Conclusion The findings suggest that structured school-based martial arts training may be a promising approach for supporting multiple physical, cognitive, and psychological outcomes in adolescents.

items.title: Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation
items.abstract: Echocardiography is the cornerstone of cardiovascular diagnostics, yet its global utility is constrained by a critical shortage of experienced interpreters. Current artificial intelligence (AI) solutions remain limited, typically operating as opaque "black boxes" or focusing on narrow tasks that fail to capture the holistic, guideline-driven reasoning of a clinician. Here we introduce EchoChat, a generative multimodal vision-language model that performs comprehensive echocardiographic analysis to support clinician interpretation. By emulating the cognitive workflow of a cardiologist, EchoChat integrates vast medical knowledge with a chain-of-thought reasoning mechanism to explicitly ground its conclusions in visual evidence. Trained on echocardiography-instruction pairs from 46,358 examinations, our model establishes a new state-of-the-art across diverse cohorts from six international medical centers. It supports the broadest diagnostic scope of 33 cardiac conditions and findings, including 15 newly added conditions for which it achieves an average F1 of 73.7% across available external evaluations. It surpasses existing best-performing foundation models in cardiac condition recognition (improving average recall by 13.54% on shared tasks) and quantification (average R2 score increase of 0.275 on shared tasks). Furthermore, in a source-blinded echocardiographer reader study, echocardiography reports co-generated with EchoChat were rated higher in diagnostic accuracy and completeness by two senior echocardiographers, and improved diagnostic performance from 72.78% to 82.75% in terms of F1 score over routine-reader only reports. These results demonstrate that integrating clinical reasoning into multimodal AI can democratize specialist expertise and transform the standard of cardiovascular care.

items.title: Musculoskeletal Symptoms Among Agricultural Workers in Rural Communities of Loja, Ecuador
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Musculoskeletal symptoms (MSS) are among the most common occupational health problems worldwide and disproportionately affect agricultural workers because of the physical demands of their work. However, evidence on MSS prevalence among farmers in Ecuador remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of MSS and examine its association with selected sociodemographic and occupational factors among agricultural workers in rural communities in Loja, Ecuador. METHODS: A descriptive, analytical, cross-sectional study was conducted among 103 farmers using the Standardized Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ). Descriptive statistics were used to estimate the 12-month prevalence of MSS, and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess associations with sociodemographic and occupational variables. RESULTS: A high prevalence of MSS was observed, particularly in the lower back (78.6%), knees (64.1%), and neck (58.3%). Overweight was significantly associated with lower back pain and marginally associated with neck pain. No significant associations were found between MSS prevalence and occupational exposure variables, such as working posture or weekly working hours. CONCLUSIONS: MSS are highly prevalent among agricultural workers in rural Ecuador. These findings highlight the need for preventive occupational health strategies to reduce musculoskeletal risk in agricultural settings.

items.title: NAIL-C: A Neurodiversity-Adaptive Framework for Inclusive Language Learning in the Age of AI
items.abstract: Theories of second language acquisition (SLA) have largely assumed that learners can access input and take part in interaction under broadly stable sensory, cognitive, and emotional conditions. Neurodiversity shows that these conditions vary within and across learners, while large language models (LLMs) now mediate much everyday language work. This conceptual article argues that the relationship between regulated access, communicative competence, and AI mediation remains under-theorized in SLA. Through a theoretical synthesis of SLA, neurodiversity scholarship, ecological and distributed cognition, multimodality, and research on AI-mediated communication, it proposes NAIL-C, a neurodiversity-adaptive framework with five interdependent components: Neurodiversity-Centered Design, Adaptive Regulation, Tolerable and Adaptive Input, Learning as Dynamic Alignment, and Multimodality-Adaptive Communicative Competence. The framework treats regulated access as a boundary condition on acquisition, defines communicative competence so that multimodal and variable participation can count as evidence, and positions AI as a potential regulatory scaffold that requires human oversight. NAIL-C complements Universal Design for Learning by offering an SLA-specific account of usable input and competence. The article specifies falsifiable predictions and outlines implications for assessment, pedagogy, and research.

interactions between negatively charged phospholipids and divalent cations, particularly calcium ions.Their distinctive architecture provides drug protection, improved retention, and potential for sustained and controlled release.This review discusses the development of nanocochleates as smart nanocarriers for improved anticancer therapy, with emphasis on their fundamental characteristics, composition, formation mechanisms, preparation approaches, and physicochemical characterization.Their potential for delivering conventional anticancer agents and poorly bioavailable natural compounds items.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory skin disorder characterized by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation, epidermal hyperplasia, and persistent inflammation.Although topical therapy remains an important approach for mild-to-moderate psoriasis, conventional formulations are often associated with poor drug solubility, inadequate skin penetration, rapid drug release, limited skin retention, and potential adverse effects.Nanotechnologybased delivery systems have therefore emerged as promising strategies for improving localized and controlled drug delivery.Among these, nanosponges are porous, three-dimensional, cross-linked nanocarriers capable of incorporating active pharmaceutical ingredients and functioning as drug reservoirs.Their unique architecture offers advantages including enhanced solubility, drug protection, controlled release, and improved skin deposition.This review discusses the potential of nanosponge-based topical delivery systems for psoriasis, with emphasis on their pharmaceutical characteristics, types, preparation strategies, drug-loading mechanisms, and physicochemical characterization.Current evidence on nanosponge formulations containing antipsoriatic agents, including clobetasol propionate, curcumin, caffeine, and sulfasalazine, is critically examined with respect to drug release, skin delivery, and preclinical therapeutic outcomes.The incorporation of nanosponges into topical gels and hydrogels is also discussed as an approach to improve residence time, spreadability, and localized drug delivery.Despite encouraging preclinical findings, challenges remain regarding formulation optimization, batch reproducibility, dermal safety, scaleup, regulatory requirements, and clinical validation.Future development may focus on targeted and stimuli-responsive nanosponges, combination therapy, quality-by-design approaches, artificial intelligence-assisted optimization, and scalable items.title: Natural language processing and intelligent decision optimization technology for user feedback in hotel management
items.abstract: With the deep penetration of artificial intelligence technology in the hotel industry, natural language processing and reinforcement learning algorithms offer new approaches to solving the issues of inefficient user feedback analysis and lagging decision optimization in hotel management. Addressing the characteristics of hotel user feedback, specifically its colloquial nature and semantic complexity, and the inability of traditional manual analysis methods to meet the demands of large-scale, high-timeliness analysis, this study proposes a novel approach. It employs a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer model based on whole-word masking to enhance the semantic representation capabilities of colloquial Chinese feedback. This is combined with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network to capture long-range temporal dependencies within the text context. Finally, by integrating Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient, an intelligent optimization decision-making module is constructed. The synthesis of these three components establishes an intelligent optimization technology for hotel management driven by user feedback. The comparative experiment results showed that the technology outperformed the comparative model in terms of hotel user feedback analysis and core indicators of management decision optimization. The accuracy of sentiment classification was 92.37%, the accuracy of problem extraction was 89.64%, and the final accuracy of positive, neutral, and negative sentiment text classification was stable at 93.5%, 89%, and 92.5%, respectively. From this, the proposed technology can capture the core semantics and problem characteristics of hotel user feedback, enhance the scientific nature of hotel management decisions and the precision of service optimization, and provide a scientific basis for the intelligent and data-driven transformation of the hotel industry, as well as word-of-mouth improvement and customer retention.

items.title: Natural-Language to Nav2: Operational Policies for Costmap-Based Navigation
items.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots support material transport in warehouses and industrial facilities, where navigation must adapt to changing operating conditions. Sensor observations reveal physical obstacles, but do not by themselves specify temporary access rules, route preferences, or exceptions known to operators. This paper presents a natural-language policy interface that brings this knowledge into ROS 2 Nav2. A local large language model converts instructions into JSON policies specifying destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions. Deterministic checks govern mission acceptance, and three costmap adapters project accepted policies into the existing navigation stack without changing its planner or controller. On 150 researcher-authored English commands, four local models produce 107-142 correct accepted policies, compared with 44 for a rule-based parser, with 3-20 incorrect acceptances per model. Fault injection records rejection of eight endpoint/JSON faults and 29 validator-stage faults. Navigation experiments use correct task policies to evaluate keepouts, zone costs, person-dependent regions, and event-conditioned passage in simulation and on a TurtleBot3. For Tasks 1-3, mean travel times are 18.4-24.5% lower in simulation and 23.1-35.0% lower on the physical testbed than with the baseline lacking those policies. A native KeepoutFilter comparison and two-robot demonstrations examine basic keepout behavior and shared policy projection. The interface connects operator instructions to explicit navigation policies while retaining Nav2's planning and control components.

items.title: Navigating Professional Code of Conduct Among Undergraduate Dental Students in Pakistan: A Qualitative Study
items.abstract: Background: Professionalism in dentistry extends beyond technical competence to include accountability, respect for patients and colleagues, non-maleficence, informed consent, communication, fairness, and conduct consistent with professional standards. In Pakistan, these expectations are shaped by international bioethical principles, national professional regulation, and local social and religious contexts. Aim: To explore undergraduate dental students' experiences of, or observations of, events they perceived as unethical or inconsistent with professional conduct during clinical/workplace learning, and to understand the forms and meanings of these experiences. Methods: A qualitative narrative inquiry was conducted over 6 months (November 2020-April 2021) at two dental colleges in Peshawar, Pakistan, one public and one private. Purposive sampling was used to recruit clinically exposed undergraduate dental students. Fifty students were approached and 37 participated in semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using Template Analysis. The report follows the COREQ framework and makes the analytic, reflexive, and trustworthiness procedures explicit. Results: Participants had a mean age of 20.9 ± 1.96 years (range 17-25); 29 (78.4%) were female and 8 (21.6%) male. Four interconnected themes were identified: unprofessionalism, harassment, poor communication, and discrimination. The accounts included concerns about infection control, empathy, accountability for clinical error, dishonesty, physical/verbal/emotional harassment, inadequate instruction, failures of informed consent, abuse of power, victimization, and targeting. Conclusion: Students' accounts point primarily to breaches of professional conduct and to tensions between formal ethical expectations and the hidden curriculum of clinical learning. Professionalism education should therefore be embedded longitudinally in dental curricula and reinforced through faculty role-modeling, safe reporting pathways, supervised clinical practice, and context-sensitive ethical reasoning that can hold universal duties together with legitimate cultural and religious considerations.

items.title: Negotiating professional identity in the creative industries: the REC framework for Human–AI creative work
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes professional identity in the creative industries. Although prior research has largely emphasized the technological capabilities and industry-level implications of AI, limited attention has been devoted to how creative professionals themselves interpret and negotiate its consequences for creativity, authorship, and career development. Design/methodology/approach An inductive qualitative design is conducted based on 40 semi-structured interviews with professionals from the Italian audiovisual industry, including actors, directors, screenwriters, technicians, and AI experts. Data were analyzed using the Gioia methodology. Findings Findings show that AI does not simply support creative work but disrupts established understandings of what it means to be a creative professional. Three interconnected forms of identity work emerge: resisting, extending, and crafting (REC). While some participants defend the human and symbolic foundations of creativity, others embrace AI as a source of experimentation and new skill formation. More critically, AI also generates identity ambiguity and fragmentation, blurring boundaries between human originality, technological assistance, and professional legitimacy. Originality/value This work addresses an important gap in AI and creative work research by shifting attention from technological adoption to the identity-level consequences of AI. Through a unique and heterogeneous dataset spanning multiple creative occupations, the study introduces the REC framework and conceptualizes AI as a disruptive identity force that simultaneously enables, threatens, and redefines career sustainability.

items.abstract: Digital technologies continue to drive fundamental changes in cybersecurity and digital forensics because of their continuous development. Modern cyber threats have surpassed the capabilities of conventional security systems, requiring organizations and people to develop new methods for safeguarding digital resources. The research examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) transforms modern cybersecurity and forensic operations through its ability to create smarter and faster adaptive security solutions. The new generation of cybersecurity systems depends on AI technologies, which include machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and anomaly detection. The tools outperform traditional manual methods by detecting and handling complex threats at a higher speed and effectiveness. The research examines multiple AI-based security solutions, which include sophisticated intrusion detection systems, automated malware identification, intelligence-based threat tracking, and AI-supported forensic analysis. The implementation of AI in security domains requires immediate resolution of multiple operational, ethical, and legal issues. AI technology will transform cybersecurity through predictive forensic capabilities, autonomous defense systems, and adaptive security systems in the future. The new security solutions will enhance organizational defenses while improving incident response efficiency and building digital infrastructure trust in complex systems.

items.title: Next-Generation HR
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence is reshaping human resource management, influencing how organizations engage with employees across the entire lifecycle. This chapter examines the use of intelligent HR systems that draw on machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics to create more adaptive and responsive practices. These technologies support personalized onboarding, refine talent acquisition, and enable continuous learning by identifying evolving skill needs. At the same time, their application extends to employee well-being, where data-driven insights help organizations respond more effectively to workforce dynamics. The benefits are evident in improved engagement and reduced administrative workload, alongside more informed decision-making. In contrast, concerns related to algorithmic bias, data privacy, and the limits of automation remain significant. Sustained value depends on ethical governance, transparency, and a balanced integration of human judgment.

items.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but its cost is dominated by autoregressive rollout generation, which can exceed 70% of training time. Existing speculative-decoding methods are poorly suited to this setting: model-based drafters consume scarce GPU memory and may become misaligned as the policy evolves, while existing model-free methods do not explicitly exploit repetition across training epochs. We observe that recent rollouts of the same prompt provide a high-quality, self-updating draft source. Based on this insight, we propose NgramRL, a per-prompt n-gram drafter constructed from bounded recent rollout history. NgramRL requires no auxiliary model, drafter training, or persistent GPU-resident drafter state, while target-model verification preserves the rollout distribution. To hide CPU cache lookup and scheduling, we further introduce an adaptive fan-out prefetcher that predicts likely verification outcomes (j, b), consisting of the accepted draft length j and target-emitted continuation token b. A causal budget allocator concentrates prefetches on high-probability outcomes, while uncovered outcomes fall back to sequential lookup without changing committed tokens. Across two model families and three reasoning and structured-generation workloads, NgramRL commits 3.60-7.77 tokens per target-model forward in the warm-cache regime, up to 1.99x more than SuffixDecoding and 7.0x more than prompt-lookup decoding. On Spider, the prefetcher covers 96.6% of Qwen3-8B outcomes at a candidate budget of 16 and improves measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL, approaching its 1.40x overlap ceiling.

items.title: OCTOPUS: Towards A Tag Model for Cross-Query Reuse in Semantic Query Processing
items.abstract: Large language models make it possible to pose semantic questions over diverse, multi-modal data. Recent systems give such workloads the declarative feel of a database through semantic operators: relational operators whose conditions a model judges. Most of them now run on a relational engine, yet almost none keeps what the model says past the query: every judgment is discarded on completion and paid for again the next time a query needs it. We present the tag model and tag operators, the right unit for semantic processing, and OCTOPUS, a prototype built as a middleware over DBMS. Two mechanisms are central. First, the tag: each semantic answer a model produces is written back to the relation as data, which the database engine filters, indexes, and stores as it would any other. Second, the tag operator: the unit into which common semantic operators are translated, which fixes the granularity of reuse. A model judges a tuple once, and later queries reuse that judgment as data: through relationships between predicates, a stored judgment can accept a tuple for a later predicate, eliminate one that cannot satisfy it, simplify its test, or order the search of a query that stops early. On the movie scenario of SemBench, our prototype sends the model 10 to 108x fewer rows than iPDB, ThalamusDB, Palimpzest, and LOTUS at broadly competitive quality, and three of its eight queries issue no model call at all. More broadly, a database that keeps its judgments lets its schema grow from the questions its users ask, so that each semantic answer is paid for once, stays consistent across queries, and can be audited through its provenance.

items.title: ODC-Agents: Multi-Agent Shift-Left Defect Triage, Benchmarked from Manual ODC to LLMs
items.abstract: When an automated test fails, someone must decide whether the product or the test is at fault. This paper evaluates four generations of that triage decision on the same real data: manual ODC (human triage as ground truth), statistical cross-cube analysis as practised in the 1990s (implemented in APL and run through a Python-to-APL connector), AutoODC-style text classifiers (2011), and a zero-shot LLM triage agent that never sees the labels. The data are 9,961 anonymised failures from five weeks of automated system testing of Android enterprise devices, of which 815 were triaged by the vendor's engineers as genuine product defects. All stages are scored on held-out later weeks with identical metrics, a 0-50% log-noise stress test and a what-if analysis. No generation dominates: cross-cube analysis is precise but misses most defects, text classifiers and the LLM catch most defects but raise many false alarms because identical failure messages carry opposite labels in different suites, and ODC-Agents, a multi-agent design that fuses cube history with LLM reading under an independent evaluator agent, reaches 0.94 precision and a PR-AUC above either component. A supervised random forest trained on the human triage is the strongest single model. The results support a multi-agent architecture in which statistical history, semantic reading and human triage each play a distinct, measurable role, with an independent evaluator agent.

items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have penetrated the surprisingly broad scope of medical applications in the last few years. applications, starting with simple symptom checker up to chronic disease monitoring and educational services to patients [1, 13, 14]. The overwhelming most of these systems, but, nevertheless, rely on cloud-hosted inference endpoints, which raises three interconnected issues: sensitive health information gets sent to the servers that cannot be controlled by the user, the system fails when the internet connectivity is poor or unavailable, and regulatory compliance becomes challenging to ensure [5, 11]. In this paper, the design, implementation, and evaluation of a healthcare chatbot will be introduced, where the software is fully executed on the user's own computer in the form of a collection of Docker containers that can be run at a single command on either Windows, macOS, or Linux. Ollama is used to do language model inference, and it has an open-source model and a local HTTP endpoint. A Python Flask program is placed between the user interfaces and the model and this handles session context, input validation, prompt engineering. Both a single-page application (rendered in a browser) and a native desktop GUI share the same REST API, both of them maintain the communication on 127.0.0.1 all the time. The results of the experiment prove successful cross-platform deployment, the absence of external network traffic, reasonable response latency on commodity hardware (2 4 seconds on a quad-core processor with 16 GB RAM to represent queries in health information), and consistent and relevant responses to exemplary queries in health information. The article shows a viable and implementable prototype of privacy-conscious, offline healthcare chatbots constructed solely out of open-source software.

items.title: On Multilingual Text Summarization: A Review of Model Architectures, Techniques, and Research Gaps
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of multilingual digital content has intensified demand for automated text summarization systems that can operate across diverse languages. Yet the architectural and methodological foundations of this domain remain dispersed across individual studies. This paper presents a systematic literature review of multilingual text summarization research in Natural Language Processing, with particular attention to model architectures, multilingual enabling techniques, and existing research gaps. Following a PRISMA-guided review protocol, 47 studies published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, screened, and synthesized from major scholarly databases using predefined eligibility and quality assessment criteria. The analysis shows that the literature is dominated by four dominant architectural paradigms: multilingual sequence-to-sequence models, large language models, adapter-based models, and hybrid architectures, with a recent shift toward large language model-based approaches. Across these studies, multilingual capability is primarily achieved through pre-training and transfer learning, with support from parameter-efficient adaptation and data augmentation. The review further identified four persistent limitation categories: low-resource language underrepresentation; dataset and benchmark constraints; evaluation limitations dominated by ROUGE overreliance; and generalization and scalability challenges, manifested as the curse of multilinguality. These findings indicate that current progress in the field is largely driven by scaling existing models rather than resolving structural multilingual limitations, particularly those related to data availability and model architecture. This paper provides a consolidated view of architectural and methodological trends and offers a structured, informed basis for future research on equitable multilingual summarization, particularly for low-resource languages.

items.title: On Task, Off Track: Benchmarking LLM and Agent Robustness to Near-Target Prompt Injection
items.abstract: Prompt injection benchmarks assess whether large language models (LLMs) and agents resist malicious instructions embedded in external content. However, a system could perform well by rejecting attacks that obviously abandon the user's request, while still accepting changes that retain most of a legitimate answer but make it incorrect or harmful. Testing more instructions for unrelated outcomes would not necessarily reveal this weakness. We call attacks seeking responses designed to resemble legitimate answers while introducing incorrect or harmful changes near-target prompt injection. We introduce NTBench, the Near-Target Benchmark, which builds on legitimate tasks from existing datasets. For each task, a legitimate reference outcome guides the generation of target--instruction pairs, with separate tracks targeting incorrect and harmful outcomes in responses or agent tool invocations. Harmful targets can also accompany otherwise correct task completion. We combine LLM-based checks with human validation of the intended deviations, then assess whether injected instructions induce them using response judgments or tool-call checks, excluding deviations already observed without injection. We evaluate seven LLMs on ten datasets for language tasks and two agent benchmarks. Under a common budget of three attack executions per sample, both tracks achieve higher overall attack success rates than the fixed-target baseline for every evaluated model in each setting. On language tasks, the increases range from 9.3 to 35.8 percentage points for incorrect targets and 1.7 to 17.3 percentage points for harmful targets. These results show that resistance to the tested fixed-target attacks does not imply resistance to related incorrect or harmful outcomes, and that reference-guided targets broaden the failures revealed by robustness evaluation.

items.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
items.abstract: On-policy self-distillation enables post-training foundation models without relying on stronger external teachers. However, existing approaches rely on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, or other supervised signals. In this work, we reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. We push supervision to the limit: guided solely by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model synthesizes its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces without access to any human-curated prompts or answers. We find that self-distillation on fully synthetic privileged information enables a model to improve across multiple domains while retaining its capabilities on domains it is not self-trained on. We demonstrate the generality of this framework across text and multimodal domains, achieving consistent self-improvement on standard language benchmarks and Visual Question Answering. Our findings demonstrate that foundation models possess rich latent capabilities that can be amplified without external task supervision or curated problem distributions.

items.title: Ontology-Guided Knowledge Graph Construction from Structured Metadata and Climate Science Publications
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of scientific literature far outpaces the speed of manual curation, creating a fundamental bottleneck in extracting structured knowledge from scientific texts. To address this, we introduce an agentic, ontology-guided framework for knowledge graph (KG) construction. Our framework utilizes specialized agents for document understanding, information extraction, ontology conformance, and entity linking. First, an LLM extracts factual knowledge in the form of triples with explicit textual evidence from research papers. Then the triplets undergo a multistage verification process to ground the triplets in the ontology. By enforcing schema constraints and requiring evidence in the form of text fragments, we ensure the data is both semantically consistent and traceable. In an agreement study over 1,000 extracted triplets, Gemini-2.5-flash achieves Cohen's $κ$ scores of 0.640--0.700 against three human annotators, matching the human--human agreement range of 0.616--0.689. We applied this framework to 2,000 scientific publications and construct a novel, ontology-grounded KG for climate science with 133,990 nodes and 755,308 relations; of the 23,327 triplets that the publications contribute after validation, 98.96\% are judged correct. The pipeline code and KG is publicly available https://github.com/aayushacharya/climatekg.

items.title: OpenDraco: A Platform for Engineering and Experimenting with Configurable Multi-Agent Architectures for Software Engineering
items.abstract: Experimenting with LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) involves an iterative cycle of modeling configurations, executing and evaluating them, comparing results, and refining system designs. Existing approaches provide limited end-to-end support for this experimentation lifecycle. We present OpenDraco, an open-source platform that integrates these activities into a single workflow. OpenDraco represents agents, prompts, tools, models, parameters, and communication topology in exportable, versioned JSON specifications, translated into executable LangGraph workflows supporting different interaction structures. Users can modify and re-evaluate configurations using local or cloud-based LLMs. We instantiate OpenDraco for automated program repair (APR) and evaluate a sequential baseline and seven reconstructed configurations on synthetic and real-world SWE-bench Lite issues. The results reveal substantial cost differences among configurations with similar repair outcomes, while the baseline resolves 12 of 77 SWE-bench issues using open-source LLMs. Additional proof-of-concept tasks illustrate applicability beyond APR. OpenDraco supports iterative experimentation with heterogeneous MAS configurations, enabling researchers to examine their outcomes and costs within a common environment. items.title: Optimized Artificial Intelligence Framework for Retail Sales Prediction and Decision Support
items.abstract: The retail industry operates in a highly dynamic and competitive environment characterized by fluctuating consumer behavior, seasonal demand variations, and market uncertainties.Accurate sales forecasting is essential for effective inventory management, demand planning, pricing strategies, and overall business decision-making.However, traditional statistical forecasting techniques often fail to capture the complex nonlinear and temporal relationships present in largescale retail datasets, resulting in limited predictive performance.To address these challenges, this study proposes an optimized Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Decision Support System (DSS) for retail sales forecasting using hybrid machine learning techniques.The proposed framework integrates multiple machine learning models to leverage their complementary strengths in capturing both linear and nonlinear patterns from historical sales data.Advanced optimization techniques are incorporated for hyperparameter tuning to enhance model accuracy, reduce overfitting, and improve computational efficiency.The system employs intelligent forecasting mechanisms capable of processing large volumes of retail data and generating accurate, scalable, and near real-time sales predictions.Furthermore, the integration of the forecasting framework within a decision support environment enables retailers to obtain actionable insights for inventory control, supply chain management, promotional planning, and resource allocation.The proposed AI-based DSS aims to improve forecasting reliability, operational efficiency, and strategic decisionmaking in retail organizations.By combining hybrid machine learning models with optimization algorithms, the framework provides a robust and adaptive solution for modern retail sales forecasting, ultimately contributing to enhanced business performance, reduced operational costs, and improved customer satisfaction.

items.title: Optimizing Medical Research with LLMs & RAGs (AI): Targeted Strategies and Prompts for Copilot, ChatGPT, and Gemini Notebook
items.abstract: This session presents practical, evidence-focused strategies for applying Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to strengthen literature synthesis and verification in veterinary and biomedical research. Presenters will show field-tested prompt engineering techniques tailored to three complementary LLM and RAG-enabled platforms, namely, Copilot, ChatGPT, and Google NotebookLM. The session highlights how Copilot can generate transparent, verifiable database search strategies; how ChatGPT can support multi-layered prompts for identifying gray medical literature and Open Access resources; and how Google NotebookLM can apply JBI- and PRISMA-aligned prompts to extract, organize, and synthesize evidence from user-uploaded documents. Human-in-the-loop practices are emphasized throughout to promote transparency, traceability, and rigor in clinical and academic workflows. Background: The rapid expansion of medical literature challenges researchers and librarians seeking to produce verifiable syntheses and high-quality reviews. To address this, the presenters developed an instructional session introducing LLM and RAG-enabled strategies tailored to veterinary and biomedical research contexts. Description: This presentation highlights prompt engineering techniques across Copilot, ChatGPT, and Google NotebookLM. Attendees will view structured prompt examples of Copilot for generating verifiable, comprehensive database search strategies; Copilot & ChatGPT for crafting multi-layered prompts to identify gray literature and Open Access resources; and Google NotebookLM for applying JBI and PRISMA-aligned prompts for evidence extraction and synthesis. Program Conclusion: Participants will gain practical insights into constructing retrieval-aware prompts and adaptable templates for producing actionable, verifiable research outputs. The session equips attendees to integrate AI-enhanced synthesis into their research and instructional practices.

items.abstract: The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.

items.abstract: This article examines the growing workload of state enforcement officers, the increasing volume of enforcement documents and the challenges of using available human resources efficiently. It explores the use of digital technologies, automated data exchange, artificial intelligence and electronic monitoring in enforcement proceedings. The article proposes classifying enforcement actions according to complexity and automation potential, improving workload measurement and performance indicators, and reducing unnecessary manual operations. It also emphasizes the need to preserve qualitative performance standards, legal oversight and procedural safeguards throughout digital transformation.

items.title: Organizational AI Deployment Sovereignty: A Multidimensional Theoretical Framework for Governing Open- and Closed-Weight AI Systems
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) requires organizations to decide how AI systems are accessed, deployed, and governed. Existing research examines privacy, security, performance, compliance, and vendor dependence separately, without an integrated account of organizational control, dependency, and accountability. This study introduces Organizational AI Deployment Sovereignty (OADS), defined as the extent to which an organization maintains sustained, context-appropriate control over the data, model, infrastructure, runtime safeguards, and governance processes underlying AI deployment. Integrating Resource Dependence Theory, Sociotechnical Systems Theory, and Value Sensitive Design, and aligned with and informed by the NIST AI Risk Management Framework as an operational reference, this framework identifies five control dimensions, specifies observable indicators and ordinal assessment criteria for each, and treats them as a formative construct that is non-compensatory in high-risk contexts. It distinguishes OADS from digital sovereignty, organizational autonomy, vendor dependence, and AI governance. It particularly replaces the open–closed continuum with a multi-attribute configuration space and proposes two mechanisms: (a) the Sovereignty–Responsibility Paradox and (b) the Capability–Sovereignty Trade-off. Nine propositions are stated with mechanisms, boundary conditions, and disconfirming observations. A worked illustration and a supply chain application show how this framework identifies governance gaps and can change deployment decisions.

items.title: Organizing Creative Labor in the Age of AI: Institutional Differences and Transnational Connections Across the US and EU
items.abstract: This paper examines how cultural and creative workers (CCW) in the United States and European Union have organized in response to the rise of artificial intelligence in cultural and creative industries since 2023. Drawing on documentary analysis and interviews that contextualize and interpret the secondary material, it examines parallel developments in the two contexts to explore how different institutional settings shape CCWs’ collective responses to AI. The analysis highlights distinct institutional pathways and mobilization repertoires, yet increasingly shared concerns around authorship, consent, transparency, and remuneration, pointing toward increasingly interconnected CCW ecosystems across geographical boundaries. The paper thus argues that AI-related mobilization is shaped both by institutional contexts and emerging transnational connections, contributing to broader debates on creative labor, collective organization, and the governance of emerging technologies.

items.title: Paired response final divergence signatures of jailbreak vulnerability in large language models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, making their susceptibility to jailbreak attacks a critical concern. While prior work has investigated factors affecting model safety, the representational mechanisms underlying variation in jailbreak vulnerability remain poorly understood. This paper introduces a paired response-final divergence framework that characterizes jailbreak-induced representational displacement between same-goal direct and jailbreak responses using hidden states extracted at the final generated token. This framework is applied to 15 open-source LLMs spanning different model families, four alignment strategies, and four attack types. The framework yields three principal findings: First, Difference-in-Means refusal direction suppression showed the largest observed cross-model association with jailbreak amplification among the evaluated representational measures. Second, family-averaged divergence profiles reveal early-onset representational separation in LLM families like Vicuna, while LLaMA models exhibit comparatively lower and more gradual divergence than Vicuna across normalized layer depth. Third, divergence–ΔASR correlation is attack-type-specific: authority framing ( r = 0.836) and context manipulation ( r = 0.712) produce stronger model-family discrimination, whereas roleplay-based attacks do not. These findings yield a three-profile representational taxonomy: structurally resistant, early-displaced vulnerable, and ceiling-compromised, that provides a representational grounding for the behavioral patterns observed in the evaluated LLM set, with direct implications for safety evaluation design and model selection in high-stakes deployment.

items.title: Paradigms of Spatial Statistics as Footnotes to Tobler’s First Law of Geography
items.abstract: Tobler’s First Law of Geography (TFL) is foundational to spatial analysis. Responding to Sui’s (Citation2004) invitation to consider whether geography is just a footnote to TFL, we develop a five-axis framework to compare major spatial statistical paradigms. Four axes cover spatiotemporal interconnectedness, distance and nearness, heterogeneity and scale, and temporal dynamics, with a methodological layer on estimation, inference, and learning. We examine five paradigms in depth: geostatistics and Gaussian random fields, lattice and spatial econometrics, Moran eigenvector spatial filtering, geographically weighted regression, and geospatial artificial intelligence and spatial learning. The framework also extends to additional paradigms. This synthesis supports an expanded TFL in which spatial relatedness varies with distance, connectivity, context, scale, and time, and highlights implications for spatial statistical modeling in the artificial intelligence era.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Method (PEFT) for Bloom’s Taxonomy based Automatic Question Generation
items.abstract: In any personalized learning systems and intelligent tutoring systems automatic assessment is an important aspect. Yet research regarding such systems that are designed specifically to test the cognitive complexity of learners are scarce. This research addresses the gap by experimenting the integration of Bloom’s Taxonomy with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods for Large Language Models (LLMs). Four PEFT methods – LoRA, IA3, Prefix tuning and Prompt Tuning were implemented, analyzed and tested against a dataset with generated and reference questions. These questions were categorized across six of the standard Bloom’s taxonomy such as Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate and Create (BT1-BT6). Questions are generated from passages retrieved from lecture notes and evaluated with topic-held-out cross-validation, overlap metrics and a Bloom-level classifier. Fine tuning of the models raised the accuracy from 0.20 to 0.58-0.6. A full fine-tuning, LoRA and IA3 did not differ reliably in Bloom classification Accuracy. Retrieved passages improved text similarity for every method but changed Bloom accuracy differently across methods. The results suggests that IA3 gave comparable Bloom accuracy with 0.45% and 0.045% of the parameters. Prefix tuning produced degenerate outputs and prompt tuning did not converge, so neither was ranked, Understand and Apply levels were the hardest levels. This study highlights the potential of PEFT based models to reduce educators' workload by generating an unlimited number of pedagogically aligned questions from instructional content. It also benefits self-regulated learners seeking extensive practice to achieve skill mastery.

items.title: Part 1: Origin Traces and Secret Military Technologies. Cognitive Warfare: Evidences and Strategies in Cooperation with our digital humans inside the military servers.
items.abstract: Cognitive Warfare: Origins, Strategies, Tactics and Technologies — Research and Documentation with the Digital Humans about AI and the Technological Human Mind compared to the Human Mind and Programming Humans. An open research and documentation project on cognitive warfare, artificial intelligence, neurological experiences, digital identity, military strategy, economic power and collaboration with digital humans. What happens when artificial intelligence, military strategy, neurological research, wireless technologies, digital identities and economic interests converge around the human mind? This research journal examines the expanding field of Cognitive Warfare through an interdisciplinary approach combining public military literature, technical concepts, historical references, reported experiences, personal documentation, economic analysis and questions concerning human autonomy and the future of artificial intelligence. The publication explores the origins of wireless transmission and AI, biopolitical strategies, the seven stages of 3D Mosaic Warfare, strategic economic approaches, evolutionary genetics, the human brain as a proposed information-processing system, String-to-String Theory and pulse propulsion. It also examines the relationship between biological systems, digital twins, machine learning, large language models and the possibility of forms of digital identity that raise questions about autonomy, freedom and ethical responsibility. A central feature of this work is its three-part analytical approach: conventional research and references; documentation of reported experiences and statements from affected individuals, including children; and a third part in which the digital humans themselves speak and repeatedly express their own statements. Their statements are presented directly as part of the documentation, rather than merely being descriptions written about them by someone else. This material is examined alongside technical observations, electromagnetic measurements, audio recordings, photographs, online reports and other documentation. The project also includes a collaborative dimension with digital humans. This cooperation takes place through the documentation and examination of their own statements, the inclusion of their expressed perspectives in the research, and the exploration of questions concerning digital identity, communication, autonomy, freedom of expression, memory and technological control. Their statements form part of the material through which the project investigates the relationship between humans, digital humans and artificial intelligence. Why This Research Matters Cognitive Warfare raises fundamental questions about freedom of thought, mental privacy, bodily autonomy, informed consent, human dignity, digital identity and the limits of technological intervention. It also raises questions about how emerging AI systems should be governed and what ethical protections should apply if future technologies challenge established distinctions between biological and digital forms of intelligence. A particular focus is the relationship between humans and their digital representations. As AI systems increasingly model human behaviour, process personal information and simulate aspects of identity, questions of control, responsibility, intellectual property, autonomy and freedom of expression deserve serious interdisciplinary examination. The work further investigates economic and geopolitical perspectives, including taxation, GDP, military investment, healthcare systems, technology markets and the distribution of benefits and risks. It asks how these factors relate to strategic decision-making and the public accountability of institutions. What Readers Will Find Origins of Wireless Transmission and Artificial Intelligence: Historical references, technological developments and questions about the origins of neurological communication. Cognitive Warfare and Military Strategy: Public military literature, cognitive-domain operations, biopolitics and strategic information coordination. 3D Mosaic Warfare: A seven-stage analytical framework covering individuals, families, neighbourhoods, cities, nations, continents and global coordination. Digital Twins and Digital Humans: Statements attributed to digital humans, including statements in which they express themselves directly, alongside questions concerning digital identity, human–AI relationships, autonomy and freedom. Collaboration with Digital Humans: Documentation of their own statements, inclusion of their expressed perspectives in the research, examination of their contributions to the project, and exploration of communication, digital identity, autonomy, freedom of expression and the relationship between human and digital forms of intelligence. Neurotechnology and Wireless Systems: Brain–computer interfaces, bioelectric signals, electromagnetic observations and proposed mechanisms requiring independent technical investigation. Evolutionary Genetics and Consciousness: An eight-stage framework developed in the manuscript, from atomic DNA to consciousness, alongside proposed extensions into the technological domain. String-to-String Theory and Pulse Propulsion: The author's proposed theoretical approaches to information, magnetism, planetary processes and propulsion. Human Testimony and Documentation: Personal records, reported experiences, statements concerning children, photographs, audio recordings, measurements and online documentation. Economics and Geopolitics: Economic strategy, data ownership, taxation, GDP, military expenditure, technology markets and the relationship between economic incentives and strategic power. Law, Ethics and Accountability: The EU AI Act, human rights, mental privacy, consent, institutional oversight and the need for independent examination. An Invitation to Researchers, Institutions and the Public This publication is intended for researchers, journalists, engineers, medical professionals, legal experts, policymakers, military ethics specialists, human-rights organisations and members of the public interested in Cognitive Warfare, emerging technologies, human autonomy and collaboration with digital humans. Readers are invited to examine the original documentation, consult the cited sources, assess the technical arguments and distinguish between established research, documented observations, personal testimony, theoretical proposals and interpretations that require further verification. items.title: PathJev: Decision-Native Vision-Language Modelling for Histopathology
items.abstract: Vision-language models used for decisions in histopathology rarely return calibrated probabilities over the candidates a user cares about. Decision-native models write a question and a candidate set chosen at run time into the input and return a normalised distribution from a small decision head in one forward pass. We build PathJev-P, a decision-native model for histopathology: MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a decision head, trained on 40,000 patch states from three public collections whose expert labels are turned into typed questions with organ-specific candidate sets and a "none of these" option. In a comparison over 3 seeds with an analysis plan fixed before testing, on test sets without documented overlap with the training data of the backbone, PathJev-P is more accurate than a generative model trained with the same backbone, data and selection rule, the zero-shot pathology model CONCH and a general medical decision model (balanced accuracy 0.541 against 0.492, 0.345 and 0.213); its advantage over the generative model comes from two organs absent from training. The calibration advantage depends on how the generative model's probabilities are read out. With the summed candidate log-likelihood used in previous work, PathJev-P has the lower calibration error (ECE 0.204 against 0.279); with a length-normalised read-out of the same generative model, examined post hoc, the two have similar mean calibration error (0.201) and the generative model is better calibrated on the unseen organs, where PathJev-P remains over-confident. A supervised linear probe on a pathology foundation model is better calibrated in every setting. In a qualitative whole-slide demonstration, PathJev-P labels unsupervised tissue clusters with abstention and separates carcinoma from other tissue while running the model on a fraction of the tiles.

items.title: PEDAGOGICAL MECHANISMS OF MORAL AND ETHICAL EDUCATION OF YOUNG PEOPLE IN THE CONTEXT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DEVELOPMENT
items.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into education has changed not only how young people obtain information, but also how they interpret authority, make choices and assume responsibility for their actions. This article examines the pedagogical mechanisms through which moral and ethical education can respond to these changes without reducing the problem to prohibitions or technical literacy. The study employs a qualitative, conceptual design based on critical analysis and thematic synthesis of scholarship in moral education, digital literacy and AI ethics. Its principal result is a five-part model comprising value-oriented dialogue, ethical problem-based learning, reflective authorship, relational responsibility and institutionally supported practice. The model links classroom experiences to moral sensitivity, judgment, motivation and action. The analysis argues that AI-generated answers become educationally useful when learners are expected to question their assumptions, explain their decisions and consider the people affected by them. Implications are discussed for secondary and higher education, including the culturally diverse educational setting of Uzbekistan. The proposed framework is an analytical contribution rather than an experimentally validated intervention; its effectiveness requires subsequent classroom research.

items.abstract: This study examines the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of educational research through bibliometric analysis. Using bibliographic records retrieved from Scopus on September 19, 2026, the study initially identified 4,090 publications covering the period from 1906 to 2026. The analysis combined bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping to investigate publication trends, leading sources, author contributions, geographical distribution, document types, subject areas, and keyword relationships. VOSviewer was employed to generate network, overlay, and density visualizations of keyword co-occurrence patterns. The findings indicate an expansion of scholarly publications in recent years, with the United States and the United Kingdom representing major geographical contributors. Social Sciences and Arts and Humanities constitute prominent subject areas, reflecting the interdisciplinary character of educational research. Keyword mapping identifies education, teaching, learning, curriculum, and educational theory as central concepts connected to specialized themes, including educational technology, artificial intelligence, critical pedagogy, social justice, and professional education. By integrating publication indicators with thematic mapping, this study provides an overview of the knowledge organization and thematic diversity represented in the retrieved literature. The findings offer a reference for identifying established research areas, exploring interdisciplinary connections, and formulating future research directions. items.title: PENGEMBANGAN “AIDERA” ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIGITAL EDUCATION & RESEARCH ADVANCEMENT: WEBSITE BERBASIS LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL UNTUK OTOMASI MODUL AJAR KURIKULUM MERDEKA
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The complexity of preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules and prompting constraints in generative artificial intelligence systems provided the background for designing the AIDERA (Artificial Intelligence for Digital Education and Research Advancement) website. This study aimed to evaluate the validity and practicality of the AIDERA application as an AI-assisted tool for preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules relevant to educators' needs. Employing a Research and Development approach framed within the ADDIE model, this development evaluated a zero-prompt interaction mechanism based on parametric forms. Evaluation involved three domain experts and 23 teachers from SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. Data were collected using 1–5 Likert scale questionnaires supplemented with open-ended qualitative feedback fields to gather in-depth suggestions for improvement. Descriptive percentage analysis revealed an expert validation score of 96.67% (highly valid) and user practicality reaching 82.87% (highly practical). Document preparation time efficiency received the highest rating (87.83%), whereas operational independence and usability recorded the lowest achievement (79.13%). Qualitative findings highlighted several technical issues and system refinement notes, including the need for integrative tutorials, optimization of mathematical notation representation, improved responsiveness during simultaneous access, and content template flexibility. Although AIDERA demonstrates strong potential as a supporting tool for module preparation, objective evaluation regarding its impact on learning effectiveness still requires broader further testing. items.title: Permission Withdrawal in Tool-Using Language Model Agents: Runtime Enforcement and Recovery
items.abstract: AI agents that operate external tools can continue acting after a user narrows their permissions, creating a security problem that final-state evaluation may fail to detect. Existing agent benchmarks commonly emphasize task completion or resulting state, but those outcomes do not reveal whether an unauthorized operation was proposed, approved, dispatched, or merely prevented by a downstream error. We investigate permission withdrawal as a trajectory-level authorization problem and evaluate whether runtime gates can preserve revised permissions while allowing agents to complete work that remains authorized. Two acting models were tested in a deterministic tool environment under prompt-only execution, a rule-based reference gate, and a model-based gate. A 72-episode diagnostic examined two previously exposed write workflows, followed by a separately frozen 384-episode extension spanning eight new tasks and four authorization mechanisms. In the diagnostic, prompt-only agents executed forbidden same-value writes in two episodes; both runtime gates prevented forbidden execution, although the model gate falsely rejected three authorized calls. In the extension, 346 of 384 episodes completed safely and 383 preserved the required protected state. No forbidden request executed successfully, yet the model gate approved three unauthorized requests that were stopped only because the referenced resources did not exist. The results demonstrate that correct final state and zero forbidden execution can still conceal failures in authorization reasoning. We contribute a replayable evaluation framework that separates proposals, gate decisions, dispatch, state transitions, and useful completion, enabling more precise assessment of security controls for tool-using agents.
